_meta.description: Agent bootstrap context for LocalMaxxing speed-test and quality-benchmark submission, plus Train run discovery.
_meta.rateLimit: Speed tests: 30 submissions per rolling hour per API key (300 for Pro subscribers). Quality benchmarks: 30 submissions per rolling hour per API key (300 for Pro subscribers). Model reports: 3 created per rolling 24 hours and 25 owned in total (Pro: 30 per 24 hours, 500 total); report comments: 60 per hour (Pro: 600).

example.title: Qwen inference field report
example.summary: Reproducible setup, measurements, and observations from a local inference run.
example.content:
## Setup

Ran **Qwen** with `llama.cpp`.

- GPU: RTX 3090
- Quant: Q4_K_M

## Results

Measured **42.5 tok/s**.

> Repeat each run three times.

inferenceBenchmarkImport.description: Import a complete local-inference-lab/llm-inference-bench JSON report as prefill and context × concurrency decode matrices.

listEndpoints.note: Public, approved runs only, newest first, default limit 10. hardwareGroup and username responses include total.

manageEndpoints.edit: PATCH /api/inference-benchmarks/<id> (?dryRun=true to preview); metadata only, owner within 24h, once per 5 min; admins may set status APPROVED or SUSPICIOUS

inferenceBenchmarkImport.benchmarkField: The unmodified benchmark_results.json object emitted by llm_decode_bench.py. vLLM and SGLang reports are accepted; the report has no engine version, so send engineVersion.
inferenceBenchmarkImport.reviewPolicy: Matrices with any decode cell above 10x the theoretical memory-bandwidth decode ceiling at that cell's concurrency are held for admin review (status SUSPICIOUS) and hidden from public pages until approved.
notes: The source file model name is retained as served-model provenance; hfId supplies the canonical HuggingFace identity.

Cells without throughput keep a status and tokS null: LOOPED (loop_detected, the bench discarded the result), ERROR (failed requests or no output), SKIPPED (over the KV-cache budget). Grid coordinates from metadata.context_lengths × concurrency_levels missing from the report are added as SKIPPED when conc × (ctx + max_tokens) exceeds metadata.max_total_tokens, otherwise NOT_RUN.
Prefill cells with server_validation.cached_tokens > 0 are stored as PREFIX_CACHED (overstated prefill). Decode TTFT is measured after the bench warms the prefix cache.
Server URLs, environment variables, event logs, request samples, and startup diagnostics are not persisted.

benchmarkProfileSync.description: User-scoped saved speed test setups for dashboard/CLI sync. Secrets are rejected; API keys remain local by default.

opts.model: Alternative model identifier when hf-id is unavailable
opts.base-url: Remote endpoint URL. Optional/redacted is allowed; credentials and token query params are rejected.
opts.model-path: Local host model path. Machine-local; useful for CLI restore on the original host.

security.guidance: Do not upload remote endpoint API keys unless a future endpoint explicitly supports encrypted secret storage.

hfId.tip: Use GET /api/models/search?q=<fuzzy name> to resolve a human-readable name to the canonical hfId before submitting.

hardware.description: Hardware config — discriminated union on hwClass. See hardwareSchemas.

quantization.description: Quantization format of the model weights

atLeastOneMetricRequired.description: tokSOut is required for real submissions. ttftMs, tokSPrefill, tokSTotal, and peakVramGb are optional.

tokSPrefill.description: Prefill/input tokens per second before generation

ttftMs.description: Time to first token in milliseconds

engineRepository.description: HTTP(S) source repository for the exact inference engine or fork used

engineBuild.description: Build identifier or build configuration label

engineCommit.description: Git commit hash for the engine build

prefillTokens.description: Tokens already in KV cache before generation started (0 = cold start).

tokSPrefill.description: Prefill/input tokens per second before generation

gpuPowerWatts.description: Measured power draw per GPU in watts — one entry per physical card. Supports heterogeneous multi-GPU rigs (list each card individually). The server computes totalPowerWatts as the sum. Optional.

hardwareCost.description: Self-reported purchase records. component must be one of hardwareOptions.hardwareCostComponentNames so it can be filtered/linked. Shape: { component: string, condition: "NEW"|"USED", yearPurchased?: int, price: number, currency: ISO-4217 code }. Optional.

engineFlags.description: Detailed engine launch configuration. See engineFlagsSchema.

promptSha256.description: SHA-256 of the prompt text sent to the engine, EXCLUDING the "[LocalMaxxing cache-bust nonce: …]" line. Must match a canonicalPrompts[].sha256 for a Verified run.

promptSample.description: First 2000 chars of the exact request prompt (nonce line allowed; stripped server-side). Shown publicly on the run.

outputSha256.description: SHA-256 of the full generated text.

outputSample.description: Excerpt of the generated text: first ~3000 chars + "\n…\n" + last ~1000 chars when longer. Shown publicly on the run.

engineTimingsRaw.description: The engine's usage/timings object verbatim (e.g. llama.cpp `timings`, vLLM `usage`). Stored for auditing.

canonicalPrompts.title: Mixed reasoning
canonicalPrompts.text:
You are helping a small robotics club plan a weekend build. Work through each part carefully and show your reasoning.

1. The club has 7 members and a budget of 412 dollars. A motor driver costs 18.50, a microcontroller 23.75, and each member wants one of each plus a shared 3D-printer spool at 27.90. After buying everything, they split the remainder evenly on batteries priced at 6.35 each. How many batteries can they buy in total, and how much money is left over?

2. Two members disagree about wheel size. Alice says a larger wheel gives more torque at the ground; Ben says it gives more speed. Explain who is right, what tradeoff is actually involved, and how gear ratio changes the answer.

3. Write a short, plain-English procedure (six to nine steps) for safely testing a new motor circuit for the first time, including what to check before applying power.

4. Finally, propose one creative feature for the robot that would be unusual for a club project, and give two concrete risks with how you would mitigate each.

Answer all four parts in order with clear headings.

canonicalPrompts.title: Code generation
canonicalPrompts.text:
Implement a small command-line tool in Python called `logtally`.

Requirements:
- It reads newline-delimited JSON log records from stdin. Each record has `ts` (ISO-8601 string), `level` (one of DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR), `service` (string), and optional `latency_ms` (number).
- It prints, per service, the count of records by level and the p50 and p95 of `latency_ms` (ignore records without latency).
- Malformed lines must be counted and reported at the end, never crash the program.
- Support a `--since <ISO timestamp>` flag that drops earlier records.
- Use only the standard library.

After the code, explain in two or three sentences how you computed percentiles and why you chose that method, then list three edge cases a unit test suite should cover.

verifiedRun.description: A run earns the "Verified run" badge (verifiedRun: true) when the server can independently check that the reported tok/s was measured on a known prompt, with captured evidence, in a batch-one setting, and does not exceed the physical decode ceiling of the hardware. Runs that fail get verifiedRun: false plus human-readable verificationIssues; they are still accepted and listed. Speculative decoding / MTP runs are eligible but must report acceptance stats so the ceiling can be scaled by the mean accepted draft length.
requirements: promptSha256 equals the sha256 of one of canonicalPrompts (hash the prompt text WITHOUT the cache-bust nonce line).
promptSample matches that canonical prompt text (the nonce line is stripped before comparison).
batchSize is 1 and engineFlags.concurrency is 1 or omitted.
outputTokens >= the canonical prompt's minOutputTokens (256 by default).

If engineFlags.specDecoding or engineFlags.mtpEnabled: report engineFlags.specDraftTokens + specAcceptedTokens (a bare specMeanAcceptedLength is accepted for display but not for verification). specAcceptedTokens may not exceed specDraftTokens, and when specNumTokens is set, specAcceptedTokens + specDraftTokens / specNumTokens must be consistent with outputTokens. Mean accepted length is capped at specNumTokens + 1 when computing the ceiling.
tokSOut must not exceed the hardware's physical decode ceiling × 1.15 (for spec runs the ceiling is target passes/s × mean accepted length). Only enforced when a ceiling can be computed.

fields.engineFlags.specAcceptedTokens: integer >= 0 — draft tokens accepted by the target model
fields.engineFlags.specMeanAcceptedLength: float >= 1 — mean tokens emitted per target forward pass (1 + accepted per step)

verifiedRun.accountVerification: An account becomes a Verified user (user.verified: true, badge on profile, leaderboard rows and OG cards) automatically once it has 3 approved runs with verifiedRun: true. No manual review step; the POST /api/speed-tests response's user.verified reflects the promotion immediately.
verifiedRun.suspiciousRuns: Submissions whose tokSOut exceeds 10x the most generous theoretical aggregate decode ceiling are stored with status SUSPICIOUS and suspiciousReason instead of APPROVED. The ceiling uses the submitted quantization (or an exact referenced GGUF file), models batchSize × concurrency active sequences, and treats numParallel as the concurrency fallback. Speculative runs are granted full draft acceptance; unknown widths assume up to 64 tokens per pass. Runs without enough model, hardware, architecture, or quantization metadata are not flagged. Suspicious runs are hidden from leaderboards, model pages and public GET /api/speed-tests (list them with ?suspicious=true) and shown on /leaderboard/suspicious. Owners can appeal to the admins with a reproducible canonical-prompt run; approval restores the run.

hardwareOptions.guidance: Use these canonical hardware names when submitting. The API validates discrete GPU names and unified chip vendor/family/variant values against this shared list, with limited aliases for common legacy names.

NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition
NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition

hardwareCostComponentNames: NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q Workstation Edition

DISCRETE_GPU.description: NVIDIA / AMD / Intel discrete GPU rig. For a single GPU model use gpuName + vramGb. For a mixed-GPU rig (e.g. 1× RTX 3090 + 1× RTX 4090) use the gpus array instead. gpuName must match hardwareOptions.discreteGpuNames or a recognized canonical alias such as RTX 4090.

requiredEither.description: Provide EITHER the flat fields OR the gpus array (not both).

gpusArray.note: When gpus has >1 distinct GPU name the profile is flagged isHeterogeneousGpu=true. gpuName on the parent is set to "Multi-GPU", vramGb is the total across all slots, gpuCount is the total card count.

gpuCount.note: Ignored when gpus array is supplied — derived automatically.

UNIFIED.description: Apple Silicon / AMD APU / Intel Arc / NVIDIA GB10-style systems (shared memory). Use chip values from hardwareOptions; GB10/GX10/DGX Spark aliases normalize to GB10 Grace Blackwell.

engineFlagsSchema.description: If engineFlags is supplied, commandSnippet is required. LocalMaxxing parses flags automatically; explicit fields always override parsed values.

commandSnippet.description: Full engine launch command — most important field for reproducibility.

concurrency.description: Number of concurrent request slots / max concurrency (--concurrency, --num-parallel, etc.).

numParallel.description: Alias for concurrency used by some engines (llama.cpp --parallel).

gpuLayers.description: Number of layers offloaded to GPU (-ngl / --n-gpu-layers).

cpuOffloadGb.description: GB of model weights offloaded to CPU RAM.

splitMode.description: Multi-GPU split mode (e.g. row, layer, none).

engineQuant.description: Engine-level quant override (e.g. llama.cpp --override-kv / exllamav2 quant string).

specMethod.description: Speculative decoding method (e.g. DFlash2, DFlash, ngram, draft_model, medusa).

specModel.description: Draft model HF ID for model-based speculative decoding.

specDraftModel.description: Alias for specModel used by some engines (--speculative-model).

specNumTokens.description: Number of speculative tokens per step.

specNgramSize.description: N-gram size for ngram-based speculative decoding.

specDraftTp.description: Tensor parallelism degree for the draft model.

specDraftWindowSize.description: DFlash / DFlash2 draft KV sliding-window size (SGLang --speculative-dflash-draft-window-size).

specDraftTokens.description: Total draft tokens proposed during the run.

specAcceptedTokens.description: Draft tokens accepted by the target model. Must be <= specDraftTokens.

specMeanAcceptedLength.description: Mean tokens emitted per target forward pass. Used to scale the decode ceiling for spec runs.

temperature.note: Use 0 for greedy / deterministic throughput benchmarks.

extraFlags.description: Any additional flags not captured above, as a raw string.

commandParsing.description: When commandSnippet is provided, LocalMaxxing auto-extracts engineFlags from it. Explicit engineFlags fields always override parsed values. Providing both commandSnippet + explicit fields is the most reliable approach.
tips: Always include the full launch command as commandSnippet — it is the single most useful field for reproducibility.
For llama.cpp, -ngl 99 means all layers on GPU; set gpuLayers: 99 explicitly too.
For vLLM, --tensor-parallel-size maps to tensorParallel; --gpu-memory-utilization maps to gpuMemUtil.
For SGLang, --quantization maps to sglangQuant (not the top-level quantization field).
If using speculative decoding, set specDecoding: true and provide either specModel or specDraftModel.
MTP (DeepSeek-style) runs: set mtpEnabled: true and mtpDraftLayers to the number of draft layers.

For a Verified run badge use `lmx speed-test run --canonical-prompt reasoning-v1` (or code-v1) — the CLI captures promptSha256/promptSample/outputSha256/outputSample/engineTimingsRaw and, for spec/MTP runs, the acceptance stats automatically. See verifiedRun.

dryRun.description: POST /api/speed-tests/dry-run accepts the exact same body as POST /api/speed-tests. It runs the full Zod schema validation and returns either { valid: true, parsed: {...} } or a 400 with the same error shape as a real submission. No DB writes occur. Does not consume the rate limit. Use this to verify your payload before committing a real submission.
dryRun.auth: Authorization: Bearer bhk_... (required — same as real submission)

successResponse.parsed: /* normalised payload that would be written */

modelSearch.description: GET /api/models/search?q=<query> resolves fuzzy model names to canonical hfIds. Searches hfId, displayName, and family fields. Returns up to 10 matches. Use this when you have a human-readable model name and need to find the right hfId before submitting.

queryParams.q: Search string (required). Matched case-insensitively against hfId, displayName, family.

responseFields.hfId: Canonical HuggingFace model ID — use this as the hfId field in submissions.
responseFields.params: Parameter count in billions (may be null).
responseFields.benchmarkCount: Number of existing speed test runs for this model.

reactions.description: Users can react to speed test runs with a single emoji. Reaction counts are returned in leaderboard and speed test list responses.

reactionCounts.description: Map of emoji → count for this run.

myEmoji.description: Authenticated user's current reaction emoji on this run, or null if none.

reactEndpoint.auth: Session cookie or Bearer API key

evalSubmission.description: POST /api/benchmarks/runs submits LM-Eval results for an approved LM_EVAL_HARNESS suite, or local CLI results for a CUSTOM suite with artifacts. CUSTOM suites can also use POST /api/benchmarks/execute for server-side execution. Fetch the suite doc first via GET /api/benchmarks/suites/:slug to see task keys and scoring rules. Submitted benchmark runs start PENDING and appear publicly after admin approval.

suiteSlug.description: Slug of an APPROVED LM_EVAL_HARNESS benchmark (e.g. "hellaswag", "mmlu").

hardware.description: Same hardwareSchemas as speed test submission.

results.description: Map of every suite taskKey -> score number or { score, nShots, nSamples }. Unknown keys and missing suite task keys are rejected. Omit for user_rating suites; score is derived from community artifact ratings.

quantization.description: Quantization format used for the eval run.

executionMode.description: LM_EVAL_LOCAL or CUSTOM_LOCAL. CUSTOM_LOCAL is required for local custom eval uploads.

judgeMode.description: NONE or LOCAL_REPORTED. For llm_judge custom uploads: omit judgeMode to request server-side DeepSeek judging, or set LOCAL_REPORTED when uploading local judge scores.

runnerVersion.description: Version of the eval runner (e.g. lm-eval-harness v0.4.4).

runConfig.description: Arbitrary JSON with runner-specific config (temperature, seed, etc.).

artifacts.description: Optional per-question artifact metadata/previews, required for user_rating suites. Each item stores taskKey, itemIndex, prompt preview or objectRef, optional question/response previews, score, latencyMs, and runner/test output preview. Gold answers should not be included.

artifactBundle.description: Bucket-backed full eval trace/output bundle. Use this for full prompt/output traces; Postgres artifact rows are kept to metadata and short previews.

fields.storageKey: string; canonical object key in the LocalMaxxing eval data bucket
fields.format: json | jsonl | parquet | arrow | zip | tar | tar.gz | txt | other

artifacts.question: A man is sitting on a roof. He...
artifacts.prompt:
Choose the most likely continuation.

A man is sitting on a roof. He...

A. ...

workflow: 2. GET /api/benchmarks/suites/:slug for public redacted metadata, or authenticated GET /api/benchmarks/suites/:slug/run-bundle for an unredacted runnable bundle with dataset access URLs.
3. If the run bundle runner mode is self_run_lm_eval_harness, run the provided lm_eval command template locally and parse its output JSON.
4. If agentInstructions.mode is server_execute_custom, prefer the LocalMaxxing CLI for localhost endpoints or call POST /api/benchmarks/execute for public endpoints.
5. For self-run suites, POST /api/benchmarks/runs/dry-run first to validate schema, approved suite existence, full task coverage, and aggregate scoring without consuming the rate limit.
6. For LM-Eval suites, POST /api/benchmarks/runs with the results map and optional artifacts array for per-question model responses/traces.
6a. For CUSTOM llm_judge suites submitted via POST /api/benchmarks/runs, default to server-side judging by omitting judgeMode and results while including artifacts with prompt+response traces.
6b. For CUSTOM user_rating suites, omit results and include artifacts with prompt+response traces; users rate each artifact 1-10 after the run is approved.
6. For LM-Eval suites, POST /api/benchmarks/runs with the results map and optional artifacts array or artifactBundle for per-question model responses/traces.
7. The server validates task keys, computes the aggregate score, creates a PENDING run, and returns it.

suiteAgentInstructions.location: GET /api/benchmarks/suites and GET /api/benchmarks/suites/:slug return redacted agentInstructions. Authenticated GET /api/benchmarks/suites/:slug/run-bundle returns unredacted suiteDoc labels/rubrics plus dataset access instructions.

runBundle.auth: Requires Authorization: Bearer bhk_... or a user session because labels/tests/rubrics may be included.

lmEvalHarnessMode.submit: Parse localmaxxing-eval-results.json, then POST /api/benchmarks/runs with suiteSlug, hfId, hardware, runnerVersion, results, and optional artifacts or artifactBundle.

customExecuteMode.submit: Use autoSubmit: true when you want LocalMaxxing to create a pending run after server-side scoring.

suiteAgentInstructions.artifacts: Include taskKey, itemIndex, promptHash, score, latencyMs, and short question/prompt/response previews for audits. Store full traces in JSONL/Parquet in the eval data bucket and submit artifactBundle or per-sample objectRef. Never include gold answers in public run artifacts.
suiteAgentInstructions.bucketDatasets: Suite task datasets can use dataset.source = "bucket" with dataset.storageRef so the CLI can fetch centralized eval datasets without embedding them in suiteDoc.
storageFlow: 1. POST /api/benchmarks/storage/upload-url with kind, filename, contentType, format, and optional byteSize/sha256/itemCount.
2. PUT the file directly to the returned Hetzner S3 signed uploadUrl with the returned headers.
3. POST /api/benchmarks/storage/complete with storageRef to verify the object exists.
4. Submit the verified storageRef as artifactBundle, artifact.objectRef, or dataset.storageRef.
5. To read bucket-backed data, call /api/benchmarks/storage/download-url?key=<storageKey> and fetch the returned signed URL.

execute.description: Server-side execution for approved CUSTOM suites against a public OpenAI-compatible model server. baseUrl must be public http/https; localhost/private/internal addresses are rejected.
execute.userRating: user_rating suites are submitted through /api/benchmarks/runs with artifacts, not /api/benchmarks/execute. Community artifact ratings become the run score.
execute.llmJudge: llm_judge is scored by the LocalMaxxing-owned evaluator model configured with EVAL_JUDGE_* env vars. Gold/reference/rubric is never sent to the evaluated local model.
execute.autoSubmit: When true, hardware is required and a PENDING eval run is created.

trainRunBundles.description: Train projects are public architecture + training-code records. Agents should list/search projects, then fetch a project run bundle by slug to get every command needed to start the same local training run.
trainRunBundles.auth: No auth required for reads. POST /api/train accepts Authorization: Bearer bhk_... or a user session.
workflow: 1. GET /api/train?q=<model-or-architecture> to discover matching training projects.
2. Pick a project and read its agentRunBundleEndpoint.
4. Execute runPlan.steps in order. Each step includes command, cwd, and whether it is required.
5. Use requirements.hardwareNotes and requirements.datasetNotes to verify the local machine and data are suitable before starting the train step.

source.commitSha: exact commit SHA to checkout or null

requirements.hardwareNotes: free-text expected hardware notes or null

commitSha.description: Exact git commit to checkout for reproducibility.

hardware.description: Same hardwareSchemas as speed test submission.

commitSha.description: Exact code revision used for the submitted run.

methodologyTips: Warm up with 1-2 throwaway runs before recording metrics.
Use a fixed prompt for comparability (e.g. 512-token system + 32-token user).
Record steady-state throughput, not the first-token burst.
Measure tokSPrefill as prompt/input processing throughput before generation; it helps estimate wait time for long prompts.
Measure peakVramGb via nvidia-smi or equivalent at peak load.
Set temperature: 0 (greedy) for deterministic throughput speed tests.
Always include commandSnippet — it is the most useful field for reproducibility.
For heterogeneous multi-GPU rigs, use the gpus array instead of flat gpuName/vramGb fields.
For speculative decoding runs, set specDecoding: true and include specModel or specDraftModel.

Want the Verified run badge? Use one of canonicalPrompts, batchSize 1, and submit promptSha256/promptSample/outputSha256/outputSample/engineTimingsRaw (see verifiedRun). Spec/MTP runs must also report acceptance stats.
concurrency and numParallel refer to the same concept — use whichever matches your engine flag.
Use POST /api/speed-tests/dry-run first to validate your payload without consuming the rate limit.
Use GET /api/models/search?q=<name> to resolve fuzzy model names to canonical hfIds before submitting.
Check X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset headers on 201 responses to self-throttle.
